clue.text: Having set off, keeping at a distance; one observed lions here

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to spark a reaction is to set it off
afar means at a distance
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A traveller sets off and keeps a safe distance while watching lions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' is the container signal; 'Having' is only a link, and the semicolon marks where the definition starts.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari park is a wildlife enclosure where visitors drive past and watch lions roaming.

clue.text: Almost call master stupid? He might

definitions.text: Almost call master stupid? He might

indicators.note: stupid suggests the letters are muddled into a new order
almost means one letter short, so the final letter of call is dropped

explanation.surface: Who would nearly call his master an idiot? A cheeky know-all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts CALL to CAL; 'stupid' scrambles CAL with MASTER. The whole clue doubles as the definition: a cocky person might call the boss stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart alec is a cocky know-all, just the sort to insult his superior openly.

clue.text: Maybe moulds entertaining chap's vocal style

indicators.note: vocal style tells us the phrase is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: an entertaining chap is a fun guy

explanation.surface: Perhaps a chap whose singing style shapes his entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'fun guy' matches the plural of fungus; moulds are an example, hence 'Maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Moulds belong to the fungus kingdom, so they are an example of these organisms.

clue.text: Have lunch here after training

parts.note: reads like a gym tip, but training means boarding a railway train, where a carriage serves meals

explanation.definitionFit: A dining carriage on a railway service is where passengers eat once aboard.

clue.text: List of staff voting to tour Scottish town

indicators.note: to tour is to travel round, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a poll is a vote
Ayr is a town on the west coast of Scotland

explanation.surface: A list of employees is drawn up by ballot before a trip to Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to tour' is the container signal. Ayr is a seaside town in Ayrshire, on Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A payroll is the roster of employees a firm pays.

clue.text: Stimulate umpire, taking her up over last of calls

parts.note: ref, short for referee, is an umpire

indicators.note: over here signals one piece set into the other
in a down clue up means the word her is written from the bottom upward
last of picks the final letter of calls

explanation.surface: Someone livens up the umpire by asking a woman to review the final calls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses her, reading upward in a down clue; 'over' sets the last letter of calls inside that reversal, just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To refresh is to revive or invigorate, which is to stimulate.

clue.text: Some of these chores seem repetitive

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Housework feels monotonous because the jobs keep coming round.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo is to repeat, so things that echo seem repetitive.

clue.text: Marks for oral in Russian?

parts.note: looks like exam scores in a language test, but Marks spoken sounds like Karl Marx, whose follower in the Soviet state is meant

explanation.definitionFit: A Marxist in Soviet Russia was a party member following Marx's political doctrine.

clue.text: Confess, with pained expression, the joke's over

parts.note: ow is the exclamation of someone in pain

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words

explanation.surface: Someone admits, wincing, that the gag has run its course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses the joke word, as a down entry read upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is an idiom meaning to admit or confess.

clue.text: Pardon woman for pinching some tables?

indicators.note: pinching means squeezing something inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: Amy is a woman's name
a nest of tables is a set that stack inside each other

explanation.surface: A woman is forgiven for stealing some furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinching' looks like theft but is the container signal. A nest of tables is a set of small tables that slot under each other.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesty is an official pardon granted to offenders.

clue.text: Signaller appears tart, maybe holding meeting

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a flan is an example of an open tart
AGM is short for annual general meeting

explanation.surface: Someone sending signals turns up looking like a floozy at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' tempts as a loose woman, but it is the pastry: FLAN holds AGM, an annual general meeting. 'appears' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagman uses flags to signal, at a racetrack or on the railway.

clue.text: Courting criticism, if it's much shorter than necessary

parts.note: a suitor courting someone pays them attentions
a pan is a harsh review, criticism

explanation.surface: Someone wooing invites a rebuke if the romance is cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: something that is far too brief, as a restless child's focus is.
explanation.definitionFit: A short concentration window is the classic example of a measure too brief for what a task demands.

clue.text: Time motorists had to skirt one great forest

indicators.note: to skirt is to go around the edge, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: the AA, Automobile Association, is the British motorists' organisation
I is the Roman numeral for one
G is short for great, as in G-G-grandfather

explanation.surface: Drivers once took a long detour round a huge woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to skirt' wraps AA, the Automobile Association, a British motoring body, around I and G.
explanation.definitionFit: Taiga is the vast coniferous forest of northern Russia and Canada.

clue.text: Way to take trick, clearly appearing behind

parts.note: overt means plainly visible, clearly appearing
rump is the backside, a behind

explanation.surface: A card player clearly leads with a trick from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: To overtrump is to play a higher trump than one already played to the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtrumping wins a card-game trick by topping an earlier trump.

clue.text: Going into process of connection that real problem posed?

definitions.text: Going into process of connection that real problem posed?

indicators.note: a problem posed means the letters are set awkwardly, jumbled into a new order

parts.note: linking is the process of connecting

explanation.surface: Tackling a real problem means joining up ideas in an unexpected way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going into' has LINKING join THAT REAL; 'problem posed' scrambles all fifteen letters. The whole clue describes the thinking method too.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral thinking means approaching a puzzle indirectly, making unexpected connections.

clue.text: Siege engine deployed there, but about to be captured

indicators.note: to be captured means to be taken inside, so one piece goes within
deployed means spread out and arranged, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: c, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A medieval weapon is set up there, though it is about to fall to the enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' rearranges the letters of there and but into TREBUHET; 'to be captured' is the container signal for C, short for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: A trebuchet is a medieval catapult with a counterweight used to batter castle walls.

clue.text: Plough through a translation from Latin

definitions.meaning: the Plough is a star pattern in the northern sky, part of a larger constellation
Ursa Major in Latin means the big she-bear in English

explanation.walkthrough: The Plough (the Big Dipper in North America) is part of Ursa Major. 'through' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The constellation containing the Plough has the English name rendered from Ursa Major.

clue.text: Deal with obstruction in pipe, perhaps, with minimal mess

definitions.text: Deal with obstruction in pipe, perhaps
definitions.meaning: a whistle is a kind of pipe, and clearing a blockage would clean it
a phrase meaning perfectly neatly, without fuss

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means spotless or done neatly; literally it means to unblock a whistle.

clue.text: Showed contempt for hesitation in speech, having drink

indicators.note: in speech says the word is to be heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: to sniff at something is to show contempt for it
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone sneered at another's stammering while having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in speech' signals that the contempt word is heard, not spelt. 'for' and 'having' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A snifter is a small drink of spirits, or the balloon glass for brandy.

clue.text: Two brutes living at no 74, originally

parts.note: a wolf is a wild beast, a brute
a ram is a male sheep, another beast

explanation.surface: Two beasts share a house at number 74.
explanation.walkthrough: Element number 74 is tungsten; its symbol W comes from this older name for it, hence 'originally'. 'Two' says 'brutes' gives two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Tungsten, the element at atomic number 74, was formerly called by this name, which supplies its symbol W.

clue.text: Endlessly agitate and dispirit wartime leader

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: to churn is to agitate, as milk for butter
to chill is to dampen spirits, to dispirit

explanation.surface: Someone keeps stirring up and depressing a leader in time of war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' drops the final letter of the agitate word. Winston Churchill led Britain in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston Churchill was British prime minister through most of World War II.

clue.text: Recent development in manufacture of clutches

definitions.text: Recent development in manufacture of clutches

parts.words: Recent development in manufacture of clutches
parts.note: reads like car engineering, but a clutch is a batch of eggs and what has just hatched from it is a young bird

explanation.definitionFit: A newly hatched young bird is what a clutch of eggs has most recently produced.

clue.text: When to make new observation, with first of stars out

definitions.text: When to make new observation, with first of stars out

indicators.note: out means the letter goes missing from the word

parts.note: a sight is something observed

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of stars

explanation.surface: Astronomers make fresh observations once the stars come out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes the letter picked by 'first of'. The whole clue also describes when astronomers watch the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Darkness after sunset is when stars appear and can be observed.

clue.text: Dope's upset, having eaten old fruit

indicators.note: having eaten means taking something inside, so one piece contains the other
upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: dope is slang for a drug

explanation.surface: A druggie feels sick after eating some old fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns DRUG to GURD; 'having eaten' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourd is the hard-skinned fruit of plants such as squash and calabash.

clue.text: Have some assets left?

parts.note: reads like asking whether funds remain, but left means bequeathed in a will to someone

explanation.definitionFit: To inherit is to receive property bequeathed by someone who has died.

clue.text: Put off boarding unusual form of transport

indicators.note: boarding means getting on board, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: rare means unusual

indicators.note: off means the letters have gone wrong, out of their order

explanation.surface: Delayed boarding of some unusual vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges the letters of put into PTU; 'boarding' is the container signal. Transport here means ecstasy, not travel.
explanation.definitionFit: Being transported with joy is a state of ecstasy, one sense of transport.

clue.text: Winger needed English strip for debut

parts.note: a kit is a sports team's strip, the uniform worn on a debut

explanation.surface: A wide player needs the England shirt for a first appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer but means a bird of prey; strip is British for a team's playing kit.
explanation.definitionFit: The kite is a bird of prey, a winged creature.

clue.text: Wood one may recall, making traditional stand

definitions.text: Wood one may recall, making traditional stand

parts.words: Wood one may recall, making traditional stand
parts.note: Sir Henry Wood founded the London Proms concerts, where audience members traditionally stand in the arena

explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a long-running summer season of London concerts with cheap standing places.
explanation.definitionFit: A promenader is a standing audience member at the Proms, the concerts Henry Wood founded.
